PHOTOVOICE: AN INNOVATIVE TOOL TO ENHANCE THE
ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE OF GRADE 12 STUDENTS IN GENERAL
BIOLOGY-I
Rheena Janelle E. Udan 1
Lea Ann P. Alegre 2
Jason M. Yap 3
1Student Teacher: BSEd-Science, Gordon College
2Master Teacher I: Senior High School, Regional Science High School III
3Program Coordinator: BSEd-Science, Gordon College
ABSTRACT
As a part of the Learning Continuity Plan (LCP) of the Department of Education,
K-12 Curriculum was restructured into the Most Essential Learning
Competencies (MELCs) resulting to the removal of several learning
competencies which made it difficult for students to connect lessons to other. In
this sense, the researchers aimed to adapt a methodology with the objective to
enhance the academic performance of the students in General Biology-I, called
Photovoice. Thus, the researchers administered a one-shot pre-test and post-test
that covered three topics which were identified as the least learned competencies
namely, Cell Cycle, Cell Transport Mechanism, and Cellular Respiration, to
assess the performance of the students before and after the intervention was
employed. A one-sample T-test was used to analyze the data gathered, where in
results showed that there is a significant difference between the pre-test and
post-test scores. This showed that there was an improvement in the students’
academic performance. However, a Pearson product moment correlation
revealed that the perception and post-test scores of the students have no
significant relationship due to different factors that may have contributed to their
performance. Nevertheless, the increase in the mean scores during the pretest
and posttest could not be neglected. The study recommends lengthening the
implementation of PhotoVoice to promote learning through real-life
experiences. Moreover, it also recommends giving full identification to the
results of this study to design more innovative instructions and strategies to
further improve teaching-learning process.
Keywords: Photovoice, Academic Performance, General Biology I
INTRODUCTION
Department of Education (DepEd), in response to the challenges the
pandemic had on education, had developed the Learning Continuity Plan (LCP).
Under this LCP is the implementation of remote learning which allowed flexibility
13

in time and place of students’ learning, including, but not limited to, the use of
technology. Though Information and Communications Technology (ICT) had
already been integrated to classrooms prior to pandemic, the situation made both
the teachers and students heavily relied more on the use of technology, particularly
smartphones, laptop, tablets, and other gadgets. Statista (2022) reports that there
are currently 6.648 billion smartphone users worldwide and 79 million in the
Philippines as of 2020. The two-year implementation of remote learning had
greatly influenced the smartphone dependence of the students (Saadeh et al., 2021;
Serra et. al., 2021).
Biology, like other science subjects, is a practical-oriented discipline
which seeks to develop the scientific inquiry and problem-solving skills of
learners. However, as a part of the LCP, K-12 Curriculum was streamlined into the
Most Essential Learning Competencies (MELCs) which was identified as the
competencies that a learner needs and important for them to acquire to have a
successful life. Many learning competencies were removed making it hard for
some students to connect present lessons to other concepts which was supposedly
included in the curriculum. Because of this, teaching Biology became challenging
because of the lack in practical or hands-on activities for the past two (2) years. To
enable the students to fully grasp the lessons, teachers need to create learning
environments that will associate the biology concepts with their real lives. It was
observed by the researchers that during Biology classes, learners show more
interest, and they easily understand the concepts when it is connected on what they
see on their daily lives.
The above information caught the attention of the researchers and thought
to adapt a methodology with the objective to enhance the academic performance
of the students in Biology, called Photovoice. Photovoice was first introduced by
Wang and Burris in 1992. It was utilized as a tool in the classroom to facilitate
substantial reflections using digital photography (Bazemore-Bertrand, 2021).
Through photovoice, students will make reflections and analyze their perspectives
to come up with descriptions evident in photos and images they have taken
(Titular, 2019). Additionally, photovoice can be utilized to encourage students'
critical thinking and the development of other abilities such as expressing opinions
and views, igniting creativity, honing research skills, fostering relationships with
others, and attracting attention (Andina-Díaz, 2020; Ciolan & Manasia, 2017;
Liebenberg, 2018, Simanjuntak, 2020). According to several studies, photovoice
can offer creative ways to develop lessons, and when used properly in the
classroom, it can successfully engage students and improve learning (Mildred, et.
al 2021, Aboulkacem, et. al, 2022).
Studies show that presenting students with activities where they could
connect what was being taught inside the classroom to their personal lives made
14

the learning experience more meaningful and increased their academic
engagement. In the process of PhotoVoice, the participants, who were also
observed to be having a hard time expressing themselves, will use voice recording
instead of the traditional written description. The said intervention was guided with
rubrics for both picture-taking and verbal descriptions and was strictly based on
the identified least learned competencies, namely Cell Division, Cell Transport
Mechanism, and Cell Respiration. Thus, with the aim to enhance the academic
performance of Grade 12 students of Regional Science High School III in General
Biology, the researchers adapted this method in the teaching-learning process.
STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM
This study aims to determine the PHOTOVOICE as An Innovative Tool
to Enhance the Academic Performance of Grade 12 Regional Science High School
– III Students in General Biology-I for the S.Y. 2022-2023. Specifically, it sought
to answer the following questions:
1. How may the respondents’ perception of PhotoVoice as a tool in
understanding and mastery of General Biology concepts be described?
2. How may the respondents’ performance in General Biology be
described before and after using the PhotoVoice?
3. Is there a significant difference between the students’ performance in
terms of Pre-test and Post-test before and after using Photovoice?
4. Is there a significant relationship between the perception and the
respondents’ performance after using the PhotoVoice?
METHODOLOGY
Research Design
The study aimed to determine whether the PhotoVoice is an effective
innovative tool in Enhancing Academic Performance of Grade 12 RSHS-III
students in General Biology-I. The researchers used Quantitative-Descriptive as
the method of research.
According to an article recently published by Crossman (2018),
Quantitative research is a structured way of collecting and analyzing data obtained
from different sources. It involves the use of computational, statistical, and
mathematical tools to derive results. It is conclusive in its purpose as it tries to
quantify the problem and understand how prevalent it is by looking for projectable
results to a larger population.
Descriptive research is used in a wide variety of research methods that
aims to describe a population, situation, or phenomenon accurately and
15

systematically (McCombes, 2022). It is concerned with the conditions, differences,
and relationships that exist, opinions that are held, processes that are going on,
effects that are evident, or trends that are developing (Best & Kahn, 2014).
Respondents
The participants for this study consist of the Grade 12 students of Regional
Science High School-III enrolled during the school year 2022-2023. Particularly,
thirty (30) students from the different sections who were distinguished to be
struggling in certain concepts in General Biology as shown in Table 1.
Based on the results of the First Quarter Exam and the classification of
grades, these students were identified who are in need of learning intervention and
need to be recovered. They were the respondents as they are the students whose
grades fell under the satisfactory level (80-84).
Table 1: Distribution of Respondents

Gauss 6 20

Total 30 100
Research Instrument
This study utilized two (2) instruments, the pre- and post-test and the four
(4) point scale questionnaire on photovoice. In the first instrument, the pre-and
post-test consisted of 30-item questions regarding Cell Division, Cell Transport
Mechanism, and Cellular Respiration. This was administered to the students before
and after employing PhotoVoice.
The second instrument was the Likert Scale questionnaire which include
statements that assessed the students’ perception towards the use of PhotoVoice as
a learning tool which was given to the respondents after the post-test. This consist
of three parameters: (1) Convenience, Interest, Ease, and Effectiveness, (2)
Measurement and Academic Achievement, and (3) Communication and
Interaction.
Statistical Treatment of Data
16

The data gathered were recorded, tabulated, and will be analyzed through
statistical treatment using SPSS. The researchers used the descriptive, inferential
statistics and one shot experimental of Pre and Post test.
Descriptive statistics are used to summarize data in an organized manner
by describing the relationship between variables in a sample or population (Kaur,
et. al., 2018). This was used to describe the academic performance of the students
based on the pre-test and post-test results and the students’ perception towards the
use of PhotoVoice as a learning tool. The researchers utilized the following
descriptive statistical tools:
1. Mean. This was used to determine the average Pretest and Posttest scores
and the final weight of each item on the students’ perception in using
PhotoVoice.
2. Weighted Mean and Descriptive Rating. These were used to describe the
perception of the students in using Photovice. Based on the total scores,
the students’ perception will be quantified as follows:
Table 2: Score, Range, Descriptive Rating, and Interpretation

3. Shapiro-Wilk Test. This was used to test the normality of the data
collected. This normality test is required to determine the appropriate
statistical tool to be used to analyze the data. If the Sig. value of the
Shapiro-Wilk Test is greater than 0.05, the data is normally distributed.
If it is below 0.05, the data significantly deviate from a normal
distribution.
Inferential statistics is used to derive estimates about a population and draw
conclusions on the data based on hypotheses testing methods (CFI, 2022). In this
17

study, this will be used to test the hypothesis of the study. Particularly, the
difference of the students’ Pretest and Posttest scores before and after using the
Photovoice and the relationship between the students’ performance after the use of
Photovoice and the perception of the students. The inferential statistical tool that
will be used in this study are as follows:
1. One-Sample T-test. This was used to determine if there is a significant
difference between the students’ performance in terms of Pretest and
Posttest scores. The required level of significance is 95%.
2. Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation. This was used to test the
significant relationship between the students’ perception of PhotoVoice
and their perception in using it as a learning tool. This statistical tool was
used to determine whether the increase in the post-test scores are related
to the usage of PhotoVoice.
Results and Discussion
Table 3 shows that students have strong agreement that PhotoVoice helped
them with their performance in terms of Convenience, Interest, Ease, and
Effectiveness with a mean of 3.317, Measurement and Academic Achievement
with 3.333, and Communication and Interaction with 3.260. The Over-all, the
average weighted mean of 3.303 implies that PhotoVoice improves their over-all
understanding of the concepts covered, facilitates and enhances the interaction and
communication among the students, and contributes positively to their learning
experiences. The findings of this study is in line with the study conducted by
Younis (2021) which revealed that students perceived PhotoVoice as a stimulating
element in their learning experiences as they had to re-evaluate their ways of
thinking and doing things.

an improvement on the academic performance of the learners based on the mean
scores. This is in line with the study conducted by Anwar (2021) where results
indicated that there is also an increase in the students’ pre-test and post-test scores
indicating that PhotoVoice helped to improve their academic performance.

distribution, the researchers decided to use parametric test to test the difference,
specifically, one-sample t-test.

used by the researchers to analyze if PhotoVoice has any effect towards the
performance of Grade 12 students. Results revealed that the posttest scores
(M=14.800, s=2.058) after the intervention are higher than pretest scores
(M=13.833, s=2.937) before the intervention. Using these data, it is observed that
the post-test had significant difference for it is higher than the pre-test. In addition,
the computed p-value that is 0.000 is lower than the level of significance that is
19

0.05; hence, these data reveal that there is a significant difference between the
conducted pre-test and post-test, rejecting the null hypothesis. These findings
corroborate the results obtained by Anwar (2021) where there is a significant
difference after having treatment by PhotoVoice indicating that students who were
taught by using PhotoVoice achieved better score.

Table 7 presents the Pearson Product Moment Correlation between the
respondents’ perceptions and performance after using the PhotoVoice. As shown,
there is no significant relationship between the posttest scores and perception based
on the p-value of 0.341, thus, null hypothesis is not rejected. This result implies
that there may be different factors that contributed to the increase of the mean
scores of the students other than PhotoVoice such as the students’ personality,
academic traits and background and teacher’s capabilities. Though perception may
not be related to the students’ performance as revealed after using the PhotoVoice,
the increase in the mean scores of the pretest and posttest could not be neglected.
The result implies that students’ perception may not reflect their post-test scores
due to different factors or variables.

Conclusion
Based on the findings, the researchers made the following conclusions:
1. PhotoVoice generally improves the students’ over-all understanding of the
concepts covered, facilitates interaction and communication, and
contributes positively to their learning experiences. Based on the weighted
mean obtained from the three (3) parameters, namely Convenience,
Interest, Ease, and Effectiveness, Measurement and Academic
Achievement, and Communication and Interaction, it respectively
indicates that students strongly agrees that PhotoVoice helped them with
their performance.
20

2. There is an increase in the performance of the students as results showed
that post-test scores were higher than pretest scores based on the mean
obtained from the scores. This just implies that PhotoVoice helped
improve their academic performance.
3. There is a significant difference between the pre-test and post-test scores
of the respondents based on the results obtained from the statistical
analysis. Hence, the intervention used is found out to enhance the students’
academic performance.
4. There is no significant relationship between the students’ posttest scores
and perception. With a p-value of 0.341, the null hypothesis is not rejected.
The result implies that students’ perception may not reflect their post-test
scores due to different factors that contributes to the increase of the mean
scores of the students other than PhotoVoice such as students’ personality
traits and background and teacher’s levels of experience.
Recommendations
Based on the conclusions, the researchers recommends the following:
1. Lengthen the implementation of PhotoVoice as a teaching and learning
tool to observe its effectiveness for a longer period of time.
2. Educators may consider using PhotoVoice in teaching other science
concepts to promote learning through real-life involvement to the students
in order to further enhance their academic performance.
3. The curricular implementors may utilize the results of this study by giving
full identification and understanding of the students’ perception and
learning experiences from PhotoVoice to help them design other
innovative instructions and strategies to further improve teaching-learning
process.
4. Future researchers may consider using experimental research where there
is a control and experimental group to build on this study and further
investigate the effectiveness of using PhotoVoice alone on the target
participants to further enhance the validity and reliability of the study

WHERE ARE THEY NOW? A TRACER STUDY OF SCIENCE
EDUCATION GRADUATES OF GORDON COLLEGE 2017-2022
Kylene Andrea R. Alim 1
Arturo C. Serdena 1
Kristoffer Paul C. Obispo 2
1Researchers: BSEd-Science, Gordon College
2Research Adviser: BSEd-Science, Gordon College
ABSTRACT
This tracer study aimed to determine the employability and graduates' rating
of their academic program from 2017 to 2022. It is a descriptive-quantitative
survey utilizing the modified Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
Graduate Tracer Study Questionnaire. Out of 71 Bachelor of Secondary
Education (BSED) Science graduates from 2017 to 2022, there were only 53
(75%) who participated. The findings revealed that graduates of the BSED
Science program had a good employability rate, and the majority of them have
found employment in fields linked to their undergraduate degrees.
Additionally, the outcomes demonstrated that Gordon College BSED
Science program alumni were in complete agreement with quality teaching,
student activities engagement, learning environment, and student support
services including the BSED Science program outcomes based on the CHED
Memo No. 75 series of 2017, at the said institution. It indicated that indicators
were acknowledged and used within the organization to improve the facilitation
of a comprehensive and concretely responsive learning experience for
graduates. The study suggested that the school consistently provide effective
quality teaching, leadership, academic program dynamic evaluation, and
professional development of the teachers who play a critical role in the
implementation of an effective academic program.
Keywords: Tracer Study, Employability, Ratings, Quality Teaching, Student
Activities Engagement, Learning Environment, Student support services.
INTRODUCTION
Education is an influential step in staying competitive and enhancing
your skills. Whether you’re starting out in your career or returning to continue to
build upon your years of experience, pursuing educational training helps you keep
moving forward (Smith, 2018). Whether they seek undergraduate or graduate
degrees, they are given the knowledge and abilities they need to succeed in the
profession. To comprehend the educational sides of their employment, for
instance, they will learn best practices in teaching in a degree program in
24

education. Pursuing work aligned to their graduate course helps them to be more
productive and flexible to their workplace. Satisfaction, contentment, and
fulfillment are produced when their career and basic values are in sync. To evaluate
the program, employability and competencies acquired in the institution after
graduation, it is important to have tracer study.
Tracer studies are essential information about graduates of academic
programs at Higher Education Institutions (Dela Cruz, 2022). Higher Educational
Institutions (HEI) frequently use tracer studies to get feedback on their programs,
learn how training has helped graduates build their competencies, to monitor and
evaluate the influence of training on graduates’ employability or success. Also,
tracer studies were carried out to see whether the quality assurance of a particular
institution is successful in making its graduates more employable. The
effectiveness can be judged according to the success or failure of the graduates to
make use of their acquired skills and training for economics.
Likewise, a tracer study is a graduate or alumni survey that attempts to
trace the activities of the graduates or previous students of an educational
institution (Millington, n.d.). Tracer study is unquestionably one of the most
important elements to Determine the success of the programs or courses the school
offers. It documents the status, characteristics of employment, struggles, and extent
of applicability of skills in the current employment of the graduates (Castro, 2017).
Tracer studies enable the contextualization of graduates of a particular university
through a system that is dynamic and reliable in order to determine their life path
or movement (The Association of African Universities (AAU), 2002 and Boaduo,
et. al, 2009).
Employability could be defined as graduates demonstrating the attributes
to obtain jobs. It also relates to the employment rates of university graduates
(Sannadan et al., 2016). Trace study is crucial for Higher Education Institutions to
track the success or employment status of the graduates. In terms of graduates’
employability, it may vary in different sectors. The public sector employs workers
through the federal, state or local government and it is tax-payer funded and is
service driven. While the private sector employs workers through individual
business owners, corporations or other non-government agencies.
Numerous tracer studies have been carried out in the Philippines to track
the employability of graduates in diverse sectors. On initiatives for science
education, there are, however, very few tracer studies. Many scholars carried out
tracer studies to assess the acceptability, applicability, and alignment of the
25

graduate degree in science offered by their particular university. The study carried
out by Arbis, et al. (2023) indicated that the graduates of BSEd at their respective
institutions have high employability, and most of them landed in professions
related to their undergraduate studies. Further, the results also showed that the
institutions’ BSED program was very effective in terms of quality teaching,
student activity engagement, learning environment, and student support services.
Similar to this, Canizares (2015) carried out a local study to assess the programs
provided by the University of San Carlos by observing its graduates in the teaching
of science and mathematics. According to him, the majority of those who
completed teacher education passed the Licensure Examination for Teachers
(LET), and the majority of them are currently working as full-time, permanent
teachers.
Employers and students can compare various universities using the
graduates' ratings in order to make educated decisions about where to attend
college and from which college student to hire. Institutions that uphold a high
standard of education and turn out graduates with the necessary skills are attractive
to students and businesses. Additionally, it aids the institution they came from in
raising the standard of instruction.
Gordon College Olongapo City, Bachelor of Secondary Education Major
in Science has a graduate of over 70 students by the year of 2017-2022. From this
number of graduates the college was not able to keep the complete database or
record and whereabouts of the said graduates. As an outcome to this, the college
department wasn’t able to distinguish where the graduates are, what they do and if
their degree helped on their present job. The BSED major in science is a four-year
teacher education program that prepares secondary science teachers. The degree
program includes a significant number of chemistry and physics courses to prepare
graduates to instruct physical sciences courses, also includes biology and
environmental science. In addition to the professional and general education
courses that gave the science instructors the content and pedagogical
understanding they needed to function as professionals and improve students'
academic performance and scientific education in general, Furthermore, graduates
are required to exemplify the ability to contribute to many types of community
development using their talents and abilities, as well as the ability to care for people
and the environment in order to uphold the greater good.
The focus of this study is to trace the BSED Science Education graduates
of Gordon College from the year of 2017 to 2022. The study specifically presented
the solutions to the following questions about the respondents’ demographic
26

profile, educational background, employment status; to determine their length of
time in acquiring a first job, to also evaluate their ratings of the course in terms of
quality teaching, students’ activities engagement, learning environment, student
support services and to evaluate their suggestions or recommendations in terms of
services, facilities, learning environment and others.

METHODOLOGY
This chapter describes the methods and procedures used by the researchers
to be able to analyze and interpret the data requirements of the research. It will
also discuss the research design, respondents, the research instruments used, the
data gathering procedure and the statistical treatment of the data obtained.
Research Design
The research design that was used in this study is mixed method. It is
generally understood that, at the most basic level, quantitative research involves
the collection and analysis of numerical data, whilst qualitative research considers
narrative or experiential data (Hayes et al., 2013). Mixed methods research
combines and integrates quantitative and qualitative methods, the researcher is
motivated to develop a broader set of research skills. Training in mixed methods
research can overcome the tendency to rely on known methods and play an
important role in widening and extending our repertoire of methods (Mertens et
al., 2016).
The researcher used the Graduate Tracer Study Questionnaire provided
by Commission on Higher Education (CHED) as modified by (Ederio, et al., 2023)
and used in their study. The modified survey questionnaire has six key sections:
respondents’ profile, educational background, employment characteristics,
graduates’ evaluation of BSED Science academic program, overall rating of the
BSED Science program outcomes, and graduates’ suggestions of the graduates for
improvement of their Alma mater.
The researcher used a combination of qualitative and quantitative data
collection and techniques. The quantitative phase will deal with the graduates’
rating of BSED Science academic program in terms of quality teaching, student
activities engagement, learning environment, student services support and the
graduates’ rating of BSED Science program outcomes. In the qualitative phase, it
deals with the questions regarding to information statistically, including their
demographic profile, educational background, employment characteristics, and
28

suggestions of the graduates for improvement of their Alma mater in terms of (a)
services (b) facilities (c) learning environment and others.
Respondents
The respondent involved in this research study were the 2017 to 2022
graduates of the Bachelor of Secondary Education who belong to the four-year
curriculum program of the College of Education, Arts and Sciences of Gordon
College, this study uses purposive sampling, it is a technique for determining
research samples with specific goals and criteria to increase the representativeness
of the data collected. Purposive sampling refers to a group of non-probability
sampling techniques in which units are selected because they have characteristics
that you need in your sample. In other words, units are selected “on purpose” in
purposive sampling. Also called judgmental sampling, this sampling method relies
on the researcher’s judgment when identifying and selecting the individuals, cases,
or events that can provide the best information to achieve the study’s objectives
(Nikolopoulou, 2022).
As mentioned by Crossman (2020), This type of sampling can be very
useful in situations when you need to reach a targeted sample quickly, and where
sampling for proportionality is not the main concern.
As a researcher, it is important to study compelling populations and
compelling questions. This often involves purposive samples in which the research
population has some special significance. Most commonly used samples,
particularly in applied research, are purposive. Purposive sampling is more
applicable in exploratory studies and studies that contribute new knowledge.
Therefore, it is imperative for researchers to conduct thorough literature review to
understand the ‘‘edge of the field’’ and whether the study population or question
is a new or significant contribution. Purposive samples are selected based on a
predetermined criterion related to the research (Mweshi & Sakyi, 2020).
Research Instrument
The primary data collection instrument used in this study is a survey
questionnaire. The survey questionnaire was designed to determine additional
information regarding the factors associated with the Employability of the
graduates, and more. The survey compromises of a mixture of closed-ended
(structured) and open-ended (unstructured) questionnaires, and the research
gathered data will undergo using descriptive statistics which includes the
frequency, weighted mean, percentage and rank.
29

This utilizes Utilizing the modified Commission on Higher
Education (CHED) Graduate Tracer Survey Questionnaire, the modified
questionnaire comprised the following five major categories:
Part 1: It deals with the personal information of the respondents, which includes
profile variables like Name, Age, Sex, Address, and Civil Status.
Part 2: It deals with the educational background of the respondents with regard to
year in which they’ve graduated, highest educations studies, and eligibility they’ve
passed.
Part 3. Employment profile of the respondents of the science graduates since
2017-2021. This section aims to know their Employment Status, Sector, Length of
before employment and others.
Part 4: The further study of the ratings of graduates of BSED Science of Gordon
College in terms of quality teaching, students’ activities engagement, learning
environment, student support services and the program outcomes of BSED
Science. The overall evaluation of graduates of BSED Science program outcomes.
Part 5: Suggestions of the graduates regarding the improvement of their alma
mater in terms of: services, facilities, learning environment, improvement in the
implementation of BSED Science Program and others.
The study used a 4-point Likert Scale to determine the extent to which the
participants agreed with different statements about their experience in the Bachelor
of Secondary Education Program during their undergraduate studies and how the
BSED Science program helps them to develop as future educators. The statements
were related to the outcomes specified in CHED Memo No. 75 s. 2017. This was
done as part of a retrospective evaluation of their overall experience.
Statistical Treatment of Data
The data collected in this study will be organized, tabulated, and processed
with the help of WPS Microsoft Excel and Statistical Analysis Using IBM SPSS
Statistics (V26) was used in the analysis of the data. According to TechTarget
Contributor (2023), it is a widely used software package for statistical analysis.
SPSS was initially developed for the social sciences, but its applications have
expanded to various other fields over time. It's commonly utilized in healthcare,
marketing, education research, and more. The statistical treatments were utilized
to address the research questions which includes the frequency count and
percentage computation, mean and, descriptive rating scale (Likert scale).
Furthermore, to test the normality of the data gathered, the researchers
used the Shapiro-Wilk test of independent groups, two tailed. According to Aslam
30

(2020), Shapiro–Wilks test is popularly used for testing the normality of the data.
Also, the Shapiro-Wilk test is a statistical test used to check if a continuous variable
follows a normal distribution as stated by Choueiry (2021). Since the data was
found to be not normally distributed, the researchers utilized Mann-Whitney U test
for non-parametric. Milenović (2011) described Mann-Whitney U Test is a
statistical technique used in statistics to examine differences between two
independent groups on a continuous scale. This test is a non-parametric alternative
to the t-test for independent samples. Unlike the t-test which compares mean values
between two groups, Mann-Whitney U Test compares their median. On the other
hand, Statistics How To (n.d) described a non-parametric test as a test that
undergoes when there is no normal distribution.
Frequency Count and Percentage Computation are used to organize and
determine the distribution in the demographic profile of the respondents, which
included their age, sex, address, civil Status, educational attainment, licensure
examination for Teachers (LET) passed, and further studies of a Master’s degree
after college.
The Mean and Verbal interpretation were utilized to determine how the
participants perceived the influence of knowledge and skills within the campus
classes in Gordon College during their undergraduate studies.
Also, the p-value approach was utilized to identify any significant
differences in the variation based on the participants' employment status and
academic program in terms of the quality teaching, student activities engagement,
learning environment, and student support services of the Bachelor of Secondary
Education graduates of science from 2017-2022.

evaluation of graduates of BSED Science program outcomes.

Graduates' ratings of quality teaching (u value = 150, p-value = .092),
student activity engagement (u value = 166.5, p-value = .224), the learning
environment (u value = 199.5, p-value = .695), and student support services (u
value = 222, p-value = .852) are not significantly different from their employment
status. The language of the report suggests that graduates' employment status does
not factor into their evaluation of their degree program.
Arbis et al.'s (2023) research backs this up, finding that graduates' ratings
of academic program indicators about their current employment position show no
substantial degree of difference. According to the study's terminology, graduates'
perceptions of the quality of their academic program have no bearing on their
subsequent employment prospects. Between 2013 and 2017, they conducted a
survey to gauge program satisfaction and alumni employment success.
There was a statistically significant difference in how graduates rated the
indicators of their academic program's type of organization, including quality
teaching (u value = 376.5, p-value = .008), student activity engagement (u value =
389.5, p-value = .004), the learning environment (u value = 386, p-value = .004),

and the availability of student support services (u value = 380.5, p-value = .009).

accordance with the terminology employed in the study, there exists a correlation
between participants' evaluations of the caliber of their academic program and the
pertinence of their institution.

The respondents express a high level of agreement regarding the
effectiveness of the Bachelor of Science in Education (BSED) program in
facilitating their ability to exhibit a profound comprehension of scientific concepts
and principles, employ scientific inquiry in their instructional practices, employ
effective methods for teaching and assessing Science, and demonstrate a
substantial and comprehensive Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK) in the field
of sciences. Furthermore, the indicators also demonstrate a high level of consensus
regarding the demonstration of a fundamental and extensive grasp of knowledge
and principles pertaining to the sciences. This includes the application of scientific
principles to address contemporary issues, the utilization of scientific inquiry to
comprehend and elucidate natural phenomena, the provision of consistent
feedback to students, and the effective incorporation of suitable pedagogy and
technology across various science domains.
The primary focus is on delivering a comprehensive education that fosters
the development of learners' intellectual, psychological, social, and religious
aspects, while also promoting excellence regarding the stewardship and service of
Filipino individuals. Moreover, it serves as a catalyst for the preservation and
promotion of Filipino history, as well as the fostering of inclusivity towards diverse
worldviews and cultures within the contemporary context of the globalization
phenomenon.
The findings of the study conducted by Palestina et al. (2020) demonstrate
that teachers and educational administrators recognize the significance of
effectively implementing the curriculum in the classroom. They acknowledge that
this implementation plays a crucial role in facilitating educational services,
enhancing human resource development, improving teacher training, and
increasing productivity. Teachers have a crucial role as implementers of the
curriculum, and their exposure to and training in various professional development
programs significantly impact and shape curricular practices.
According to Pujiyati et al. (2018), the implementation of academic
programs at higher education institutions can be enhanced through effective
leadership, which has the potential to maximize productivity and exert influence
on peer relationships, collegial work, and the mobilization of support.
52

The successful implementation of academic programs in higher education
institutions is characterized by the prioritization and demonstration of desired
outcomes, skills, and competencies within the curriculum. This emphasis is crucial
in preparing undergraduate students for their transition into the workforce. The
synergy between institutional administration, the learning environment, student
support services, and pedagogical approaches employed by educators contributes
to this outcome. Arbis et al. (2023) identified several integral mechanisms that
serve as prerequisites for achieving optimal performance and enhancing the quality
of academic learning experiences.
Based on the responses, the thematic analysis revealed the following
themes:
1. FACILITIES
Laboratories: Requests for improvement in laboratory facilities, equipment, and
supplies are common. Several respondents have asked for complete laboratory
apparatus, microscopes, and materials for practical learning.
Respondent #8:"Improve laboratory facilities and equipment."
Respondent #11:"Improve the laboratory facility for better lab
instruction.”
Restrooms: Concerns about the safety, security, and conditions of restrooms have
been raised.
Respondent #18:"More safe to use restroom cubicles."
Respondent #48:"Make the comfort room door sturdy."
Classrooms: The conduciveness and conditions of classrooms have been
discussed, with some suggestions for improvement in air-conditioning and room
decor.
Respondent #13:"Hope it still air-conditioned classroom because it helps
a lot for us to study comfortably."
Respondent #39:"More conducive rooms.”
Study Areas: There are suggestions for creating additional spaces for studying,
such as student lounges or study rooms.
Respondent #15: "More available rooms for the students, Or study room
for science students.”
53

Technology: Respondents also mentioned the need for technological
improvements, like SMART TVs in labs and newer computer models in the
library.
Respondent #17: "Install SMART TV inside the laboratories to cater video
lessons etc."
Respondent #45: "Invest more in laboratory materials like microscopes,
centrifuge, etc."
Addressing these facilities concerns is essential for providing students
with a conducive and supportive learning environment. By investing in laboratory
equipment, improving restroom conditions, upgrading classrooms, providing
adequate study spaces, and enhancing technology infrastructure, our institution can
better meet the needs and expectations of its academic community. It's important
to involve students, faculty, and staff in the decision-making process to ensure that
these improvements align with their preferences and requirements.
2. SERVICES
Efficiency: The need for timely, smooth, and fast services has been highlighted,
especially concerning the enrollment process and document retrieval.
Respondent #8:"Provide timely services to cater to the needs of all
students."
Respondent #12:"Smooth and fast office/document process."
Efficiency in school operations and staff behavior are related issues that
have a big impact on how students experience school in general. Educational
institutions must put an emphasis on effective procedures while making sure that
all employees maintain professionalism and foster a friendly atmosphere for
students. Schools can give their students a more favorable and conducive learning
environment by addressing these issues.
3. LEARNING ENVIRONMENT
Inclusivity: The importance of a diverse and inclusive learning environment has
been emphasized.
Respondent #8:"Be more inclusive to the diversity of students."
Respondent #41:"It's should not be in the classroom all the time, because
learning can happen out side."
54

Teaching Approaches: Suggestions include differentiated instruction, more
hands-on activities, and the use of technology.
Respondent #6: "Be more considerate to students."
Respondent #12:"Differentiated instruction for lessons."
Classroom Ambience: Respondents pointed out that room decor could make the
environment more conducive to learning.
Respondent #17:"Decorate the rooms aligned with the room designation
to add conduciveness to the learning environment."
"Respondent #19: "Mentioning the air-conditioned rooms, it lessen the
struggle of the students coping up to a lesson or a discussion during summer or
even day time."
Education professionals, administrators, and students all share the
objective of establishing a productive and friendly learning environment. It's a
constant effort to create a welcoming, productive learning atmosphere. We can
work together to make our educational settings more inclusive, engaging, and
enriching for all students by taking into account the feedback from various
responses and participating in this debate. In order to improve the learning
environments of today and tomorrow, it is essential that we share our knowledge,
our experiences, and our creative ideas.
4. IMPROVEMENT IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF BSED SCIENCE
PROGRAM
Curriculum: Suggestions for additional subjects, broader subject matter, and
more hands-on activities have been made.
Respondent #14:"Additional subjects that may help in the program."
Instructors: There is a demand for competent, well-trained instructors who can
adapt to modern teaching techniques.
Respondent #7:"Instructors should be Education graduates and should be
accomplished teachers."
Respondent #42:"More on practical experience and training."
Collaboration between educators, curriculum designers, and institutions is
essential to improving the way the BSED Science Program is implemented. The
proposals for more subjects, a wider range of topics, qualified instructors, and real-
55

world experience are excellent places to start when improving the curriculum.
These concepts can be improved by having additional conversations and doing
research, which will open the door for a more successful and complete BSED
Science Program.
5. OTHERS
General Suggestions: These include miscellaneous feedback like having online
resources readily available, improving the canteen, and offering more courses.
Respondent #25:"Canteen food should be more cheaper."
Respondent #28:"To open other courses like engineering and
architecture."
Both the introduction of new degrees and the accessibility of canteen
meals have advantages and drawbacks. It is imperative that the institution's
leadership take these recommendations seriously, do extensive research, and hold
meaningful talks with teachers and students. In the end, achieving a balance
between financial viability, student happiness, and academic advancement will
result in a more active and effective learning environment.
This analysis provides valuable insights into the areas that need attention
for improving the educational experience in the institution.
Conclusion
Observations led to the following conclusions:
1. The respondents' profiles revealed that the majority of the respondents are
within Olongapo City, are between the ages of 22 and 33, are from the classes of
2018 and 2019, are mostly female, single, bachelors, and LET passers.
2. Using the data provided regarding the respondents' employment profile, it was
determined that:
• Most of the respondents accept their first job within less than a
month because it is relevant to their program and comes highly
recommended by their family or friends.
• Majority of employed graduates work for either public or private
organizations; the majority are regular or permanent employees, and the
majority are teachers, which is relevant to their program.
• End of contract and family concerns are the main reasons given
by unemployed graduates for their lack of employment.
56

3. Considering the data provided regarding the Gordon College institution's
evaluation from BSED Science graduates, it showed that:
• The graduates strongly agreed with the institution’s quality of
teaching, learning environment, student activities engagement and support
services.
• They also strongly agreed with the institution's BSED Science
program outcomes based on the CHED Memo No. 75 series of 2017.
4. Based on the data given regarding the employment profile in terms of:
employment status, type of organization, job relation to program; and graduates’
rating, it showed that:
• There is no significant difference between the graduates’ rating
when grouped according to Employment Profile specifically in terms of
employment status and job relation to program.
• There is a significant difference between the graduates’ rating
when grouped according to Employment Profile specifically in terms of
type of organization.
Recommendations
Based on the study and analysis of the answers of survey questionnaires
and feedbacks from the respondents, this study makes the following
recommendations:
1. Continue conducting tracer studies to track the long-term career
development and happiness of science graduates at regular intervals (e.g.,
every five years). This information can be used to spot patterns, advantages,
and potential improvement areas.
2. Examine and conduct a study of a comparable nature that includes a large
sample of graduates from various programs that include laboratory, medical,
and scientific courses and subjects.
3. Create an alumni network or group to strengthen links between the college
and its scientific graduates. Regular alumni gatherings, newsletters, and social
media groups can help with on-going communication, let people share their
successes, and offer chances for mentoring and teamwork.
4. For science students, the college ought to think about providing specialist
57

career counseling services. Workshops on creating resumes, interviewing, and
job-searching techniques specifically for jobs related to science could be
included. Alumni may also be asked to speak with current students about their
careers and offer advice.
5. Review and update the scientific curriculum frequently to make sure it
reflects the demands of the market and new developments. Ask for feedback
from alumni and business leaders on a regular basis to determine the most
important knowledge and skill areas for graduates to possess.
Regularly evaluate and improve Gordon College's science curriculum to
maintain its level of excellence and ensure that graduates are prepared for the
changing needs of the labor market.

The Journey of Becoming Professionals: The Experiences and Challenges of
BSEd Science Student Teachers through Teaching in Virtual Class
Hershelene Bueno, Abegail M. Castillon, Mark Arthur Escoto 1
Kristoffer Paul C. Obispo 2
1BSEd-Science Students, Gordon College
2Research Adviser: BSEd-Science, Gordon College
ABSTRACT
Practicum teaching is the most important aspect for becoming a professional
teacher since it provides student teachers with authentic and hands-on
experience and also allows the student teachers to put their idea into practice in
a real classroom setting. However, due to the outbreak of COVID-19, the classes
were moved virtually where student teachers also need to adjust to the new
normal setup. Thus, this study aimed to determine the experiences and
challenges of the BSEd–Science fourth year students of Gordon College during
their practicum teaching in a virtual classroom. Focused group interview method
was employed in this phenomenological qualitative research wherein the
researchers created a questionnaire that is composed of eleven (11) open-ended
questions that will identify the experiences and challenges of the fourth-year
education students majoring in Science in their practice teaching in a virtual
classroom. The findings of the study revealed the experiences of the participants
in terms of student’s performance and classroom management as well as their
challenges when it comes to student’s participation in class, with regards to their
availability of internet and devices, their environment and also with their
confidence in teaching. Data for this study were collected from 6 students of
BSEd–Science students enrolled in the school year of 2021-2022. The
researchers concluded that, teaching virtually is challenging due to
uncontrollable hindrances and disturbances that occurs during their teaching
internship, however, despite of the challenges occurred, the participants is able
to finish their practicum. Therefore, it is recommended to conduct studies that
associate additional factors and variables related to the study.
Keywords: experiences, challenges, student-teachers, practice teaching, virtual
classroom
INTRODUCTION
Practice teaching is the most important aspect for becoming a professional
teacher since it provides student teachers with authentic and hands-on experience
and also allows the student teachers to put their idea into practice in a real
classroom setting (Msangya et.al, 2016). Ulla (2016) also stated that practice
62

teaching prepares student-teachers to become qualified teachers in the future on
their own respective specialization. During this essential stage of a teaching career,
it will begin in developing the skills and adopt the values that shape one's approach
to teaching.
Practice teaching is integral to all teacher-education institution and also
teacher-education student or pre-service teachers as the conduct of this experience
allows pre-service teachers to apply theoretical knowledge learned during the
academic phase of their program (Roble & Bacabac, 2016). The practice teaching
is one of the requirements in finishing the degree in education (Ulla, 2016).
However, due to the outbreak of COVID-19, most of the schools in
Olongapo City were needed to close for the safety purposes of the students. With
that, the classes were moved virtually where student teachers also need to adjust
to the new normal setup. Hence, as an alternative to students’ teachers, they needed
to practice their teaching through online interaction with their students to continue
their practicum teaching, wherein the student teachers are expected to face various
challenges which might influence their teaching efficacy in practice.
This study was developed because of the interest of the researchers to
know the experiences and various challenges that faced by the BSEd Science
Student-teacher enrolled in Gordon College during their practice teaching through
virtual classes.
STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM
This study generally aimed to determine the experiences and challenges of
the fourth year BSEd – Science of Gordon College in performing their practice
teaching in a virtual classroom. Specifically, this study sought to answer the
following:
1. What is the profile of the participants?
1.1 Age;
1.2 Sex;
1.3 Devices used in practice teaching.
2. What are the experiences of the participants in performing practice
teaching in virtual classroom in terms of:
2.1 Student’s performance;
2.2 Class Management?
3. What are the challenges of the participants in performing practice
teaching in virtual classroom in terms of:
3.1 Student’s participation;
3.2 Availability of Devices;
3.3 Internet availability;
3.4 Environment;
63

3.5 Confidence in teaching?
4. What are the implications of the study?
METHODOLOGY
Research Design
The study employed the phenomenological qualitative research as
Chambers (2013), Phenomenology is an approach to qualitative research that
focuses on the commonality of a lived experience within a particular group. The
fundamental goal of the approach is to arrive at a description of the nature of the
particular phenomenon. Additionally, Lambert and Lambert (2012) stated that the
goal of the qualitative descriptive studies is to summarize comprehensively the
specific events experienced by the participants which are the experiences and
challenges of the fourth-year education student when it comes to performing their
practice teaching in a virtual classroom.
Therefore, the main purpose of the study was to determine the experiences
and challenges of the fourth-year education student when it comes to performing
their teaching internship in a virtual classroom.
Respondents
The population is composed of fourteen (14) participants who are
currently studying at Gordon College as fourth-year education students majoring
in Science. The researchers used the criterion sampling as a sampling technique as
it is used to select sample based on a pre-established criterion by stating the
inclusion and exclusion criteria (Suri, 2011). As a result, the total number of
participants who participated in the study is six (6) participants wherein it is
gathered using the sampling technique mentioned.
Research Instrument
In conducting the study, the researchers created an interview-
questionnaire that is composed of eleven (11) open-ended questions that will
identify the experiences and challenges of the fourth-year education students
majoring in Science in their practice teaching in a virtual classroom.
The researchers contacted the participants to ask their consent and allow
the researchers to conduct a group discussion interview for the study. Afterward,
once the consent was secured, the researchers have provided a google meet link to
further start the interview.
Statistical Treatment of Data
64

Thematic analysis will be used in interpreting and analyzing the gathered
data. As indicated in the study conducted by Braun and Clarke (2006), this type of
data analysis involves the coding of qualitative data into clusters of comparable
articles, or conceptual categories, as well as the identification of consistent patterns
and links between themes in order to arrive at a theoretical explanation for the
phenomenon under investigation.

the conflict they usually encounter is background noise, and the other conflicts are
sudden power interruption, internet connectivity, students with shocking
questions, students' participation in a group activity, the quizzes of students, and
the students itself. Wherein these conflicts are immediately resolved by the
respondents with their own skills as well as knowledge in resolving conflicts that
arise during their practice teaching. Wherein, Conflict is something that is natural
and must be experienced by every individual, it has a positive impact as well as a
negative impact (Tuimur & Chemwei, 2015). For a conflict to have a positive
impact, individuals need to have conflict resolution skills such as knowing the
source of the conflict, who is in conflict, and the right strategies and tactics to
resolve the conflict (Gibbons, 2010).

performance of the teacher. Likewise, according to Beardsley et.al (2021),
teaching confidence and preparedness can improve teaching.

Conclusion
After conducting the study, the researchers concluded the following:
1. During the entire experience of practice teaching of the participants,
anxiousness is inevitable and will be incorporated because of pressure.
Anxiety or nervousness is normal, but as they proceed in their
discussions, they can gradually overcome it.
2. At some point, doing practice teaching virtually is partly exciting and
not exciting due to different experiences in a virtual classroom. This
includes the student participation in the class.
3. Indeed, teaching virtually is also challenging because of the
uncontrollable hindrances and disturbances that may occur, such as
background noises, sudden power interruption of power and internet
connection, quality of the devices used, and teachers adding
workloads resulting to compression of time.
4. Time management is essential for a student teacher, as there are
overwhelming workloads that will occur and need to be done at the
same time.
5. Moreover, as a student teacher, mental health must not be overlooked
because there are times that they will feel exhausted and stressed. With
that, it is important to allot time to rest distress.
6. Despite multiple hindrances occurred, the participants thrive and has
survived the practicum.
83

Recommendations
This study revealed the experiences and challenges of BSEd – Science
fourth year students during their practice teaching in a virtual classroom. Based on
the summary of findings and conclusions, the following recommendations were
drawn:
1. Look at some additional factors and variables related to the experience
and challenges of student teachers who perform their practice teaching
in an online modality;
2. Use a large quantity of participants and use different program or
courses as their population to gain further accurate results as
experiences and challenges may vary;
3. Utilize the study in providing the needs of future teachers and students
in a virtual learning set-up;
4. Make further research regarding the experiences and challenges of
preservice teachers that performs their practicuum in a face-to-face
learning.

Keywords Abstract
Experiences, The research aims to identify the challenges and difficulties
challenges, encountered by BSEd-Science Students of Gordon College in
student- having physics virtual laboratories and Simulations. The research
teachers, also seeks to determine whether the virtual lab allows students to
practice boost their self-paced learning. The online interview was used as
teaching, the primary data gathering method. The finding of the study which
virtual showed that it affects the learning of the students, most of the
classroom. respondents’ experience distraction mainly, social media, house

software.
INTRODUCTION
Online class has been the new normal when it comes to our educational
setting during the pandemic and with the help of a multitude of platforms that can
be utilized to teach even with great distances, learning never stops but it comes
with difficulties that are unavoidable. The efforts of science teachers to manage
online learning have not optimized students' varied learning experiences because
science can't be learned by reading and discussion only, but also by hands-on
activities. (Wisanti et al. 2021)
According to Sypsas and Kalles (2018) Laboratory classes are essential in
Biology, Biotechnology and Chemistry, as they help learners acquire skills and
understand physical phenomena in depth. To run hands-on laboratories one needs
space, equipment and staff, so virtual laboratories can help reduce the total cost
and still complement physical presence. During this pandemic, laboratory
experiment and exercises seems harder to do due to different circumstances we are
facing within each other’s home since privileges is not similar to every student,
one might find this difficult to execute, it might be too expensive to others or it
lacks the essential skill acquisition that only hands-on experience can provide.
Many science researchers attempt to answer such a question through
87

studies that focus on the effects of computer simulations on students’
understanding of science concepts as well as on motivation. These researchers
studied the effectiveness of computer simulations from different points of view.
Some researchers have studied the efficiency of computer simulations compared
to the traditional method (Chen & Howard, 2010).
It was concluded that the developed virtual chemistry laboratory software
is at least as effective as the real laboratory, both in terms of student achievement
in the unit and students’ ability to recognize laboratory equipment, Tatli and Ayas
(2013). With this in hand, students are able to grasp concepts in chemistry without
the aid of real life or hands-on experiments due to the effectiveness of laboratory
simulations and software.
Online education has demonstrated comparable learning gains when
analyzed to those of the traditional classroom, but research is mixed when
reviewing students’ ability to manipulate tangible laboratory equipment after
participating in online experimentation. The question remains, are students who
are exclusively enrolled in online science courses equipped with the cognitive
ability to operate laboratory equipment within a physical laboratory? When
considering the optimal learning environment for science majors, educators have
discovered the blended classroom may provide the perfect opportunity to combine
the benefits of face-to-face instruction and feedback with the reinforcement of
scientific theory through technology integration. (Rivera, 2016)
Over the last two decades a great deal of educational research has been
directed towards the exploration of students' ideas and difficulties on physical
concepts and processes, Driver et al. 1985; Duit, et al. 1991). Physics simulations
on the other hand do lack the hands-on experience unlike with the chemistry
simulations which don't fully require the hands-on part to fully grasp the concepts
taught within laboratories.
STATEMENT OF THE PROBLEM
This study is conducted to identify the major difficulties and the factors
that result in the major difficulties in Physics Virtual Laboratories and Simulations
among 3rd year students of BSEd-Science in Gordon College.
This study seeks to answer the following questions:
1. Respondent profile is described by the following
1.1. Device/s used for online classes
1.2. Device/s owned for online classes
1.3. Wi-Fi or Data user
1.4. Internet Speed/Latency (megabits per second) (applicable for WIFI
users)

1.5. Signal Strength (1-4 bars)
1.6. Employment Status
1.7. Family Income (Monthly)
2. Identification of difficulties and relating them to the factors or the student’s
profile:
2.1. What are the major difficulties experienced by the majority?
2.2. What are the associating factors with the major difficulty?
2.3. How significant the difficulty is to the associating factor/s?
3. What are the student’s other queries aside from those mentioned in the
student’s profile?
METHODOLOGY
This chapter describes the study's methodologies and processes, which
were utilized by the researcher to gather, analyze, and interpret the research's data
needs. This chapter also covers the study design, respondents, research
instruments, instrument construction, data collection technique, and statistical data
analysis
Research Design
Phenomenological qualitative research design was the chosen design by
the researchers. Researchers will gather qualitative data in order to complete and
refine them. “A set of guidelines and instructions to be followed in addressing the
research problem” (Mouton, 1996:107).
For the qualitative part of the study, semi-structure virtual research is
carried out in order to reveal the opinions of BSEd Science 3rd year students of
Gordon College about utilizing virtual laboratory applications.
The characteristic feature of this design is that the study is done with one
survey questionnaire for measuring the instrument in collecting data and to reveal
the difficulties encountered by Based Science 3rd year students of the said school
in utilizing virtual laboratory application.
Respondents
The respondents of this study are the BSEd Science 3rd year students of
Gordon College, Olongapo City who were enrolled in the year 2021-2022. Among
the participants of this study, 15 were males and 6 were females.
The researcher used non-probability sampling because it was very
acceptable for this study. Non-probability sampling is a sampling technique where
the samples are gathered in a process that does not give all the individuals in the
population equal chances of being selected. There is also a risk that it may produce
89

less accurate and misleading results. But based on the capability, experience,
budget of the researcher and the time span that the research will take place, it is
more convenient and practical like most of the samples in nursing research (Polit
& Beck, 2006).
Research Instrument
The researchers will utilize online interviews by using a questionnaire
through Google Meet, Messenger Video Call, or zoom. The information that will
be collected in the survey made the study strengthen its standard. The online
interviews were conducted on current 3rd-year BSEd-Science students at Gordon
College.
The questionnaire is designed to acquire information about the experience
of the respondents on utilizing virtual laboratories in the classroom. The researcher
created the questionnaire after reviewing reference materials and thinking about
how to use the virtual laboratory in class.
Statistical Treatment of Data
The third-year BSEd-Science students' responses to the interview
questionnaire will be thematically analyzed to meet the study's data criteria. The
number of responders who answered similarly in a certain item or question will
influence the frequency of each response. The researchers gradually formed a
result based on the answers provided by the respondents.
Thematic analysis is the often-used method of qualitative research,
providing concise description and interpretation in terms of themes and patterns
from a data set. The application of thematic analysis requires trained expertise and
should not be used in a prescriptive, linear, and inflexible manner while analyzing
data (Majumdar, 2018).
Owing to its flexibility, thematic analysis, however, can never be criticized
being devoid of scientific temperament. The method of thematic analysis consist
of very specific and clear guidelines for its conduction, and these procedural
guidelines no doubt give the method a scientific vigor (Majumdar 2018), (Braun
and Clarke 2006), while propounding the six-step process of analysis in thematic
technique, have not only focused on the procedural concepts like “what”, “why”,
“when” and “how” of the method concerned but have also specified that the analyst
should have clarity and immense technical expertise to carry out the analysis
through thematic method. This touch of procedural simplicity mingled with
complex technical background gives thematic analysis a detailed yet rich flavor in
comparison to other qualitative analysis methods, and henceforth makes it the most
popular and widely used method for qualitative data analysis.
90

performing the said simulations since home setting mixes up the respondents’
tasks. Social media also has its fair share of dilemma when it comes to determining

thus home setting (environment) gives the majority or most of the challenges to
the respondents. The general studies and the research of the pedagogical
experiment confirm that the best results in learning content can be achieved by
using a mixed teaching method, i.e., virtual lab physics should only be used
together with the traditional method, choosing methodically which of the
laboratory works will be done virtually in the traditional way. As the results show
with the help of the virtual laboratory it is possible to strengthen students' ability
to read and interpret graphic information, but to learn to work with text and
understand the context, traditional methods are better. Cooperation and
communication skills are strengthened by traditional works when respondents are
forced to cooperate and help each other, which is necessary during traditional
laboratory work. (Juskaite 2019).
Environment
Research has found that learning environments play a crucial role in
student success. Several factors can affect learning ability, including seating, light,
noise, and even color. Students who study in a positive learning environment have
been shown to be more motivated, engaged, and have a higher overall learning
95

ability. On the other hand, students learning in poor environments – those that are
uncomfortable, loud, or full of distractions – will find it far more difficult to absorb
information and stay engaged. With this in mind, let’s look at how your
surroundings affect the way you study, and consider some of the best ways to
create your ideal learning environment. (Hendrix,2019)
More than one in three students could not study at home as they were
engaged in household chores during the pandemic, a regional study has found. Of
the 396 who participated in the UNICEF’s U-Report South Asia poll, the biggest
concern for more than 100 Bhutanese youth was about not having time to study at
home due to household work during the Covid-19 pandemic. The findings also saw
that almost an equal number of youths feel they were given too much schoolwork.
No or limited access to online learning, worry about the exam, and difficult to
study in the home environment were their other major concerns. (Rinzin,2020)
Technical Difficulties
Pre-existing disparities among students in terms of socio-economic status
and territorial origin have worsened. For instance, the National Conference of State
Legislatures (NCSL) has reported that 20% of college students in the US have
issues accessing effective technology such as working laptops and reliable
highspeed connection to pursue their higher education online. In particular,
students living in remote or rural areas have struggled to benefit from the
advantages of digital education. Cases have been reported of students unable to
follow their courses because of their insufficient or unstable internet connection,
inadequate resources such as laptops that bug all the time, or their impossibility to
find a calm environment to study. (Girard et al, 2021)
Communication
Students still prefer classroom classes over online classes due to many
problems
they face when taking online classes, such as lack of motivation, understanding of
the material, decrease in communication levels between the students and their
instructors and their feeling of isolation caused by online classes. Research
limitations/implications This research studied the impact from students'
perspective only as the sample was selected only from students. Originality/value
This research reached the students’ point of view in a broader way which will help
understanding the issues and provide effective solutions. This research suggested
that instructors must communicate with their students and vice versa in more
informal channels (instant messages online chat groups, audio calls, private video
calls …) in parallel with the formal channels (online platforms, email …). Finally,
instructors should encourage students to participate and study more by providing
different kind of incentives. (Alawamleh et al, 2020).
96

Physiological
The purpose of this study was to identify the impact of student psychology
on online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic. The research method uses a
qualitative research type of phenomenology. The research subjects were 30
students of Mulawarman University who were interviewed via telephone. The
research findings show that (1) students have started to get bored with online
learning after the first two weeks of learning from home, (2) considerable anxiety
on research subjects whose parents have low income, because they have to buy
quotas to be able to participate in online learning, (3) mood or mood changes occur
due to too many assignments and are considered ineffective by students.
Suggestions and recommendations from this research are the need for severe
efforts in assisting the psychological well-being of students through the
involvement of counselors and psychologists. (Irawan et al, 2020)
Personal dilemmas also have their contribution into respondents’
difficulties. This affected them in terms of coping abilities, attention span, and the
over-all feel of the online modality made them feel lazier than before during the
face-to-face era.

Conclusion
The findings were to funnel down to conclude that:
 In accordance to the profile:
 Only one respondent is working and the rest are non-working.
 Family income is enough to support data and internet
connection.
 Devices required for physics simulations are present for
everyone
 Most of the respondents’ experience distraction mainly, social media,
house chores, personal dilemmas and technical aspects like unsupportive
software.
 As for their recommendations:
 Professors’ involvement in most simulations are highly
demanded or suggested
 Collaboration or peer groups were also suggested
 Simulations must be user friendly since most of the simulations
are too outdated and has limited instructions.
Recommendations
Based on the study and analysis of the answers of survey questionnaires
and feedbacks from the respondents, this study makes the following
recommendations:
 Conduct a study that asks similar queries but in a different field
102

like biology or chemistry.
 Increase the number of respondents.
 Do more readings and study further topics regarding the current
topic.

respective fields. One examining the effectiveness of internship programs for BS in
Customs Administration students provides crucial insights for policy reform, while the
